entities.name: Ovarian endometrioma
observations: Benign ovarian manifestation of endometriosis; homogeneous low-level or ground-glass echoes on transvaginal ultrasound are characteristic.
Symptoms commonly include chronic pelvic pain that worsens cyclically before or during menstruation.
Recurrence after treatment is common; reported recurrence is approximately 21.5% at 2 years and 40–50% at 5 years after surgery.

entities.name: Endometriosis
observations: Chronic benign gynecologic disease involving endometrium-like tissue outside the uterine cavity; ovarian endometrioma is a recognized manifestation.
Laparoscopy with direct visualization and histology has traditionally been the reference diagnostic approach, although typical endometrioma may be diagnosed noninvasively with high-quality imaging.
Hormonal therapy can suppress symptoms and reduce recurrence but is not first-line for every patient.

entities.name: Symptomatic endometrioma treatment
observations: For symptomatic, enlarging, persistent, large, infertility-associated, or diagnostically uncertain ovarian endometriomas, laparoscopic surgery is a standard treatment approach; medical therapy is mainly for symptom control and recurrence suppression.
